note: Nearest fire-insurance map to the 1900 census. May 1898, four sheets. Shop names on the Hurst brick block are the labels read on sheet 2. Where a 1898 label could not be read, the 1893 name is kept.

add.name: Dwelling
add.notes: The one-story dwelling at the Davis end of block 80, East Main side, is two stories on the May 1898 Sanborn, sheet 2, lot 316. The January 1886 and August 1893 sheets show that house as one story, so the old house is taken off and this one put in its place. No family name is printed.

add.name: Dwelling
add.notes: A frame dwelling on lot 2 of block 72, the Crawford side, second lot from Hurst. The May 1898 Sanborn, sheet 2, shows a dwelling here. The August 1893 sheet shows the cigar factory and carpenter shop on this lot and does not show this house. No family name is printed.

add.name: Dwelling
add.notes: Two-story frame dwelling on the Dean side of block 81, lot 201, where the Excelsior Mills stood on the 1886 and 1893 sheets. May 1898 Sanborn, sheet 2. Still there in March 1906. No family name is printed.

add.name: Dwelling
add.notes: One-and-a-half-story frame dwelling on the Dean side of block 81, lot 201, beside the other new house. May 1898 Sanborn, sheet 2. The mill is gone on this sheet. No family name is printed.

add.name: Home Steam Laundry
add.notes: May 1898 Sanborn, sheet 2, block 81, labeled Steam Laundry on the south edge of the old mill lots. The March 1906 sheet labels it Home Steam Laundry. The 1886 and 1893 sheets show the Excelsior Mills here instead.

update.name: Bank of Bushnell

facade.photoSource: Mark's undated photograph of the 400 block of East Main, looking north, and the postcard from the 300 block.

update.notes: The Hurst corner of the 400 block of East Main, Crafford side, block 59. Mark's view looking north, and the postcard taken from the 300 block, both show this corner as a two-story red brick bank. The signs read BANK OF BUSHNELL and DENTIST. A 1900 paving petition names the Bank of Bushnell as the end of an East Main stretch, and does not give the lot. No Sanborn label for this bank was read. The corner is the one across Hurst from the 300 block. The partial grocery word farther down the block is not copied as a firm name.

facade.photoSource: Mark's postcard, East Main St., Bushnell, Illinois, from the 300 block looking north.

update.notes: August 1893 Sanborn, sheet 2, the Hurst corner room of the brick block on the 300 block of East Main, block 72. Mark's postcard shows an ornate two-story brick with a corner bay and a projecting sign, BILLIARD HALL and LUNCH ROOM. Those are sign words, not an owner's name. The May 1898 sheet reads the corner room as Photo and a room further west as lunch, so which room carried the sign is an estimate. The 1893 sheet called this corner a market.

update.name: The Democrat
update.notes: The readable cornice sign in Mark's about-1900 view looking south on West Main. The McDonough Democrat began in 1884. A 1908 paving note sends a route east on Hail to the Democrat office, which puts the office at Hail and West Main, the near end of this view. The exact bay is an estimate. The photograph is not used to call any other door a newspaper.

update.name: Grocery
update.notes: Mark's view north on the 400 block of East Main shows a sign ending in GROCERY. The letters before it were not legible, so they are not used. This is the generic word only, on an existing stand-in past the pediment.
